citations.B1: Read-then-write on `counts` races across threads/workers — two concurrent requests can both read the same count and both pass, exceeding the limit
citations.B3: use an atomic increment or per-key lock (e.g. `threading.Lock`, or a store with atomic INCR)
citations.B4: No sliding/fixed window or reset — once a user hits `limit` they're blocked forever, not per-interval
citations.B5: Unbounded growth of `counts` — entries are never evicted, so memory grows forever with new user_ids
citations.B6: with multiple workers/processes, each has its own counter, so the real limit is `limit * num_workers`
citations.B7: No input validation on `user_id`/`limit` — `None`, non-hashable, or negative/zero `limit` aren't handled
